thread.title: Need to Know: This ‘parabolic’ move for stocks has some investors nervous, but should it?

title: Need to Know: This ‘parabolic’ move for stocks has some investors nervous, but should it?
text:
7:30 a.m. ET Share 
Critical information for the U.S. trading day iStockphoto How much longer can investors hang in there? 
By Social-media editor 
Is this bull market finally starting to feel a bit top-heavy? 
According to official MarketWatch records, this marks the 698th time that very question has been asked in this space since Trump took office. But it’s hard not to ask it again, considering the “parabolic” move the market is making lately. 
“U.S. equities have already gained more in the first few weeks of January than they do in many full years,” writes Urban Carmel of the Fat Pitch blog. “The equity market is undeniably hot, and that can often lead to a period of retracement and decline, but trends weaken before they reverse, and this one has not shown any sign of weakness.” 
To bolster his upbeat case, which earned our call of the day , Carmel pointed to this set of charts from Fundstrat’s Tom Lee. He gathered a sample of eight other times the S&P SPX, -0.40% showed this kind of ”parabolic” breakout: 
Carmel pointed out in a weekend post that the S&P ended higher after the next 12 months in six of these eight instances. 
“In other words,” he wrote, “expecting the current torrid pace to continue unabated is low odds, but the gains so far in 2018 are unlikely to mark a significant top.” 
Let the good times roll, eh? Key market gauges 
Will it be another one of those peppy 2018 market days? For now, futures for the Dow YMH8, -0.44% and S&P ESH8, -0.43% are pointing to a modestly lower open. Gold GCH8, -0.75% is getting dinged, while crude CLH8, -0.83% is little changed . Asian markets ADOW, -0.02% were mixed. Europe SXXP, -0.19% is mostly lower. 
Check out the Market Snapshot column for more. 
In cryptos, bitcoin BTCUSD, -5.23% is changing hands around $11,300. Ethereum and Ripple both enjoyed double-digit percentage gains overnight, but have now slowed their roll. The chart 
MCBM [pronounced“mac-bim”...?] doesn’t really have the ring to it that FANG does, but the stocks in the clunkier acronym have actually performed better. 
Sure, Facebook FB, -1.92% Amazon AMZN, +1.41% Netflix NFLX, +3.76% and Google GOOGL, +0.15% have beaten the market, but it’s not all that surprising, since they are the leaders of the tech sector. But what about McDonald’s MCD, -0.27% Caterpillar CAT, -2.54% Boeing BA, -0.66% and 3M MMM, -0.49% ? 
Turns out, as you can see by this chart from the Felder Report , they’ve delivered stronger returns over the past two years: 
But why? “You might rationally presume that, because the stock market is known as a discounting mechanism, this surge to unprecedented valuations reflects a surge in their respective businesses,” says Jesse Felder. (Yes, I might.) “In that case, you would presume wrong.” 
Felder shows how the average sales growth for these four has actually done just the opposite, yet the stocks keep moving higher. He says one driving factor is that dividend-focused ETFs have been buying them up like crazy. The buzz 
Lots to focus on this week, but it could be a full earnings schedule and the Federal Reserve’s first meeting of the year that drives markets in the coming days . There are 125 S&P 500 companies, including 10 Dow components and high-profile tech firms, reporting. 
Hackers continue to cause problems for crypto enthusiasts. The latest heist looks like it’ll mean a big hit for Japanese exchange Coincheck , which said Sunday it would spend up to $426 million to pay back victims of a hack from last week, as Japanese regulators demand fixes . 
Ingvar Kamprad, the billionaire Swedish entrepreneur who founded Ikea when he was 17 and built it into one of the biggest furniture retailers in the world, died Sunday at 91. And the Twitter response was exactly as you’d expect it to be. 
Maybe it’s not so bad looking so bad after all for iPhone X suppliers? Shares in AMS AMS, +16.92% AMSSY, +20.88% — whose chips help power Apple’s AAPL, -1.95% FaceID feature — have been surging following an outlook raise . 
But Apple shares themselves are slipping after a Nikkei report that the company plans to halve its production target for the iPhone X. Check out: Apple earnings: Forget taxes, the $1,000 iPhone X remains the story

“It’s not about money at the end of the day. Money doesn’t equate to happiness. It doesn’t. That’s missing the whole point. You treat people like human beings” — Jay Z, when asked by CNN about what Trump has done for the black community: 
The president didn’t like it, and started a beef with this tweet: Somebody please inform Jay-Z that because of my policies, Black Unemployment has just been reported to be at the LOWEST RATE EVER RECORDED! — Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) January 28, 2018 The stat 
On Friday, the S&P closed up 1%, breaking a record streak you probably didn’t even know anything about. 
According to the Irrelevant Investor’s Michael Batnick , it’s been 94 days since the last time the S&P moved at least 1% higher, yet the broad market gauge still managed to add more than 14% during that time period. This is something that’s never happened before. 
“What do these numbers mean? Stocks have been moving higher at a snail’s pace,” Batnick writes. “What do these numbers mean going forward? Nothing.” But still... The economy 
All eyes will be on the January jobs report on Friday, but before that, there’s plenty of data to digest, including the January ISM manufacturing index, monthly car sales figures and the Case-Shiller house price index, all of which hit later this week. 
As for today, we get the personal income and outlays number for December at 8:30 a.m. Eastern followed by the Dallas Fed Survey of Manufacturing Activity two hours later. Random reads
